body: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) announced that Air New Zealand and Hong Kong International Airport (HKG) (HKIA) are the first organizations to achieve One ID Certification, with the certifications presented at the IATA World Passenger Symposium (WPS) in Macao. One ID is a set of global industry standards for using digital identity and biometrics across the passenger journey, supporting a journey where passengers confirm their identity and travel documents before reaching the airport, then pass through checkpoints using facial recognition instead of repeatedly showing their passport and boarding pass. The new certification gives airlines, airports, and governments assurance that an organization's use of digital identity and biometrics meets IATA's global One ID standards.

Organizations can be certified in one or more of four areas of activity: Digitalization of Admissibility, Contactless Travel, Biometric Handling, and Privacy, Consent, and Governance, and the certification is open to airlines, airports, and technology providers. As the first organizations to achieve One ID Certification, Air New Zealand and Hong Kong International Airport were certified across all areas applicable to their respective operations. IATA's 2026 Global Passenger Survey found that 78% of passengers would be willing to share their biometric information in order to avoid having to present physical travel documentation at airport checkpoints. "Digital identity can make travel much simpler for passengers, but only if everyone involved in the journey trusts how others verify identity, handle biometric data, and protect privacy," said Nick Careen, IATA's Senior Vice President, Operations, Safety and Security.

HKIA's self-service biometric identification system, Flight Token, has transformed the departure journey by enabling passengers to travel through key airport checkpoints using facial recognition; today, more than 80% of departing passengers at HKIA are eligible to use Flight Token across all checkpoints of the departure journey, and since its launch in 2021, more than 93 million passengers have used Flight Token to date. Vivian Cheung, Chief Executive Officer of Airport Authority Hong Kong, said achieving One ID Certification confirms that HKIA's digital identity and biometric processes align with IATA's global standards. Jeremy O'Brien, Air New Zealand's Chief Customer & Digital Officer, said the airline's trial with Hong Kong International Airport showed how digital identity could work across borders, reducing the need for documentation and queuing.
en.summary: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) announced that Air New Zealand and Hong Kong International Airport are the first organizations to achieve One ID Certification, with both certified across all areas applicable to their respective operations and the certifications presented at the IATA World Passenger Symposium in Macao.

body: 國際航空運輸協會（IATA）宣布，紐西蘭航空與香港國際機場成為全球首批取得One ID認證的機構，認證在澳門舉行的IATA世界旅客研討會（WPS）上頒發。One ID是IATA為在旅客旅程中運用數位身分與生物辨識而制定的全球產業標準：旅客在抵達機場前先確認身分與旅行文件，之後在各查驗點以臉部辨識通關，不必反覆出示護照與登機證。這項新認證讓航空公司、機場與政府能確認，某個機構使用數位身分與生物辨識的方式符合IATA的全球標準。

認證涵蓋四個領域：入境資格數位化、非接觸式旅行、生物特徵處理，以及隱私、同意與治理，開放航空公司、機場與技術供應商申請；紐西蘭航空與香港國際機場都在各自營運適用的全部領域取得認證。IATA的2026年全球旅客調查發現，78%的旅客願意分享生物特徵資訊，以換取在機場查驗點不必出示實體旅行文件。IATA營運、安全與保安資深副總裁Nick Careen指出，數位身分只有在旅程中各方都信任彼此驗證身分、處理生物特徵資料與保護隱私的方式時，才能真正簡化旅客的體驗。

香港國際機場的自助生物辨識系統Flight Token讓旅客以臉部辨識通過離境旅程的關鍵查驗點，目前超過80%的離港旅客符合使用資格，自2021年推出以來累計已有超過9300萬名旅客使用。香港機場管理局行政總裁Vivian Cheung表示，取得One ID認證證實香港國際機場的數位身分與生物辨識流程符合IATA的全球標準。紐西蘭航空首席客戶與數位長Jeremy O'Brien則表示，紐航與香港國際機場的試驗顯示數位身分可以跨境運作，減少出示文件與排隊的需要。
